data.name: Add components to a product model
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to add components to a product model (e.g. tabletop, legs, door, shelf), so that the product is built from meaningful parts that customers can configure.


Acceptance Criteria
    I can add a component with a name and code (e.g. “TOP”, “LEGS”).
    A component is linked to a chosen product model.
    I can see all components belonging to a model.
    Only admin/manufacturer users can manage components.

data.name: Add attributes to a component
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to add attributes to a component (e.g. width, height, color, material), so that customers can customize the component during configuration.


Acceptance Criteria
    I can add an attribute with: code, label, and type (ENUM, INTEGER, DECIMAL, BOOLEAN).
    For ENUM attributes, I can define allowed values.
    For numeric attributes, I can define minimum and maximum values.
    The attribute is linked to a specific component.
    I can see all attributes assigned to a component.
    Only admin/manufacturer users can manage attributes.

data.name: Add image layers to a component
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to upload image layers for a component (e.g. top, legs, doors), so that the configurator can visually display the product based on customer-selected attributes.


Acceptance Criteria
    I can upload or link an image file (stored externally or by URL).
    I can assign each image layer a view (e.g. FRONT, TOP, SIDE, PERSPECTIVE).
    I can assign each layer a z-index to define stacking order.
    I can define conditions when the layer should be shown (e.g. “COLOR = OAK_01”, “WIDTH between 1200–1600”).
    The layer is linked to a specific component.
    I can see all image layers for the selected component.
    Only admin/manufacturer users can manage image layers.

data.name: Define pricing rules for attributes
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to define how each attribute affects the price of the product (e.g. larger size = higher price, premium material = extra cost), so that the system can automatically calculate the final price of any configuration.


Acceptance Criteria
    I can specify a base price for the product model.
    I can define price modifiers on attributes, such as:
        fixed amount (e.g. +500 CZK for color “Walnut”)
        incremental amount (e.g. +1 CZK per mm of width)
        dynamic or conditional rules (future)
    I can assign price modifiers to:
        a specific attribute value (e.g. COLOR = OAK_01 adds +300 CZK),
        or a numeric range (e.g. WIDTH > 1400 adds +1000 CZK).
    The system calculates the price by:
        base model price
        sum of all attribute modifiers.
    The updated price is returned through the configuration preview API.
    Price rules are visible and editable for the manufacturer.
    Only admin/manufacturer users can manage pricing.

data.name: Customer can view a configurable product
data.notes:
As a customer, I want to open a product model in the configurator, so that I can see its options and start customizing it.

Acceptance Criteria
    I can open a URL/page for a specific product model.
    I see basic info: product name, description, and starting price.
    I see a list of configurable components (e.g. tabletop, legs, doors).
    For each component, I see available attributes (size, color, material, etc.).
    The configurator loads all data from the backend (model, components, attributes, pricing rules, image rules).

data.name: Customer sees live price and visual update
data.notes:
As a customer, I want the product preview and price to update when I change options, so that I immediately see how my choices affect the product and its cost.

Acceptance Criteria
    When I change any attribute (size, color, material…), the configurator:
        sends my current configuration to the backend,
        receives an updated price based on the pricing rules,
        receives the correct image layers for the chosen attributes.
    The total price on the page updates without reloading.
    The product image updates (layers change) to reflect the chosen attributes.
    If I choose an invalid combination, I see a clear error or validation message and no price is calculated.

data.name: Submit a request (Customer → Manufacturer)
data.notes:
As a customer, I want to submit my configuration together with contact details, so that the manufacturer can prepare a personalized offer.

Acceptance Criteria
    I can enter contact details (name, email, optional phone, optional note).
    The system sends my entire configuration, including:
        selected product model
        selected component attributes
        calculated price
        timestamp
        contact details
    After submitting, I receive a confirmation message.
    The backend stores the inquiry and links it to:
        the product model
        the configuration snapshot
        the user’s contact info
    The configurator prevents submitting incomplete or invalid configurations.
    No account is required for customers (public submission).

data.name: Manufacturer views list of requests
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to see a list of all customer inquiries, so that I can review and process incoming requests.

Acceptance Criteria

    I can open an admin page with a list of inquiries.
    For each inquiry, I see at least:
        customer name
        email
        product model name
        date/time of submission
        current status (e.g. New / In progress / Offer sent / Closed)
    The newest inquiries are shown first.
    Only admin/manufacturer users can access this list.

data.name: Prepare initial image set for testing the configurator
data.notes:
As a developer, I want to upload a small set of test image layers for one sample product so that I can verify that the configurator correctly displays and updates visuals.

Acceptance Criteria
    A test product (e.g., table) has image layers for each component.
    Each attribute option has at least one corresponding PNG layer.
    All images are aligned to the same canvas size.
    Images are uploaded to storage and linked in the database.
    The frontend can load and update these images during configuration.

data.name: Embed configurator on external website
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to copy an embed code from the admin interface so that I can easily add the configurator to my website without technical knowledge.

As a manufacturer, I want options for width/height/theme when generating the embed code so that the configurator fits my website design.

Acceptance Criteria

    Admin UI shows a ready-to-copy embed script.
    Embed script includes product ID and company ID.
    Inserting the script on any website displays the configurator.
    No backend setup required by the manufacturer.
    Changes in admin automatically propagate to the embedded configurator.

data.name: Configure domain for the app
data.notes: Buy domain and configure it for the deploy

data.name: Figma prototype
data.notes: Create a Figma prototype so that it can be tested the with real users.

data.name: Change password
data.notes:
As an admin user, I want to change my password, so that I can secure my account after the initial setup.
    The system must provide an endpoint to change the currently logged-in user’s password.
    Changing the password requires the current password and a new password that meets security rules.
    After a successful password change, existing sessions can optionally be invalidated.

data.name: Create users - members of the team
data.notes:
As an admin user, I want to create new users, so that I can give access to other team members.
    Only users with the ADMIN role can create new users.
    Newly created users receive credentials (or an invitation flow) to log in.

data.name: Create a product model
data.notes:
As a manufacturer, I want to create a new product model (e.g. a table or wardrobe), so that I can start defining what customers will later configure.

Acceptance Criteria

    I can enter a model name and description.
    The model is saved and gets a unique ID.
    The model appears in my list of product models.
    Only admin users can create models.

data.name: User setup & basic authentication
data.notes:
As an admin user, I want to log into the system using my email and password, so that I can access admin functionality.
    The system must support logging in only with valid credentials of an existing, active user.
    After login, the admin is redirected to the admin area.

As a system, I want to allow login only to registered users, so that unauthorized people cannot access the admin.
    Login attempts with unknown email addresses or invalid passwords are rejected.
    The system must not create users implicitly during login.

As a system, I want to restrict admin routes to users with the ADMIN role, so that only admins can manage product models and other admin features.
    All admin HTTP endpoints and UI routes are accessible only to authenticated users with role ADMIN.
    Non-admin users are either redirected or receive an appropriate error when accessing admin routes.

subtasks.name: Project Setup - Backend
subtasks.notes:
Create repository and project structure
    Create Git repository configurator-backend
    Initialize .gitignore (Kotlin, Maven, IntelliJ)
    Set up multi-module Maven (domain, application, infrastructure, bootstrap)
Configure Kotlin & Spring Boot
    Add Kotlin + Spring Boot dependencies in parent pom.xml
    Verify project compiles and runs
Setup Docker environment
    Create Dockerfile for backend
    Create docker-compose.yml with Postgres
    Test running backend + DB with docker compose up
Configure database connection
    Add application.yml with Postgres settings
    Add basic JPA config
    Test successful DB connection on startup

subtasks.name: Project Setup - Frontend
subtasks.notes:
Initialize React + TypeScript project
    Set up basic folder structure (components, pages, api)
    Install and configure React Router
    Create base layout (header, container)
    Add .env and .env.example
    Configure ESLint + Prettier
    Add Dockerfile for frontend + connect to docker-compose
    Add minimal placeholder pages (Configurator, Admin)

subtasks.name: Database model
subtasks.notes: Create a database model and think about all the entities that will be needed

data.name: Deploy the app
data.notes:
As a developer, I want to host the backend, database, and frontend on fully managed services (Railway, Supabase, Vercel), so that I don’t need to maintain servers or deal with infrastructure.

Acceptance Criteria
    Backend deployed on Railway.
    Database hosted in Supabase.
    Frontend deployed on Netlify/Vercel.
    Domain configured
